comment: Numeric ratchet manifest (DR-27a). Two arrays, one mechanism — tests/guards/numeric-floor-manifest.test.ts enforces both. A `floors` entry is a minimum that its test asserts; a `ceilings` entry is a maximum. Any floor or ceiling may move up or down: the entry's description and the PR body give the old value, the new value and the reason. The lean-prompts goal: the bytes that a typical run reads should not grow, and a ceiling rise states its reason (docs/reference/lean-prompts.md, Rules for every target). An older description or test comment that says a value may only rise or only fall is history; this rule replaces it. Each entry pins a value AND the number of sites spelling it: the guard requires exactly `occurrences` matches of `pattern` in `sourceFile`, so a change of one site out of several, in either direction, is caught. New entries are allowed in either array; move `floor`/`ceiling`, `pattern` and `occurrences` together with the assertion. Equality baselines (the GIT_MD_* / SKILL_* / TOTAL_* constants in tests/goldens/github-status-lines.test.ts) are exact baselines, pinned in that file, and are not registered here.

Spelled as an exact count it was the ratchet inverted — adding a payload, the thing a reviewer most wants a contributor to do, failed the suite.

Rows HOSTILE_REFS must carry — shell separator, command substitution, both flag-injection spellings, path traversal, size, the zero-numbered key an unanchored digit class admits, and whitespace. Every pinned grammar in PROVIDER_REF_GRAMMARS is driven over the whole table, so one row added widens the corpus for every provider at once and one removed silently narrows it for all of them. A FLOOR for the same reason as min-hostile-payloads.

ceilings.description: THE git.md ceiling — the one gate on dist/agents/git.md, the always-loaded half of the tracker contract/mechanics split and a term every loaded-set row below carries. Re-derived by #376 as a measured 44_163 ch plus the 80 ch general headroom, after the series close-out cut git.md by a net 94 ch. #365 (PR6), the last PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357, had closed the reservation ledger (its git.md delta was -70 ch) and set every git.md-carrying row to min(previous ceiling, measured + 80), 80 being the headroom the rows carried before the series began (82/77/73/90 ch at 5020e06). The headroom is not a reservation: any addition funds itself with a cut. The measurement follows #326's move of the PR-host operations' bodies into references/pr/{op}.md and #358's moves of non-contract text into the references each operation already loads, plus the condensed ## Principles, then #359's and #360's fixes, #362's mechanism inputs and #363's test-plan evidence op, merge-readiness evidence and CI-status fix, #364's trace map, traceability exceptions and associate-release op, #365's ensure-pr-ready caller-block inputs, and #376's close-out. No per-component decomposition of any cut is recorded — three successive re-derivations of such components disagreed once already — so measure the artifact instead: npm run build && node -e "process.stdout.write(String(require('fs').readFileSync('dist/agents/git.md','utf8').length))". May be LOWERED, never raised: a budget raised to fit the artifact is not a budget, it asserts that the current size is the current size. #393 (PR6 of epic #387) moved the Git agent's provider resolution onto the settings line and retired the mechanics-unavailable rule: git.md measured 43_832 (net -315 ch), so the ceiling fell to min(44_243, 43_832 + 80) = 43_912. #425 (the Git agent split) re-derived it downward to min(43_912, 35_474 + 80) = 35_554: the provider resolution and the tracker input contract moved into tracker/_contract.md, which a spawn reads only when it runs a tracker operation, and the provider-neutral step text of the tracker operations moved into the per-provider references; the Output section with its report cap, and the frontmatter effort and denylist, were paid for out of that cut. #445 (part 2, the Git and Tracker tool allowlists) lowered it by exactly the 251 ch the frontmatter cut took out of git.md (a 17-name denylist became a one-line allowlist): 35_554 to 35_303, the digest commit's net +2 ch on git.md leaving the headroom at 78, from 80. Re-derived by #451 (D-OP-ONE-REF, D-OP-CONTRACT-ONCE) from a measured 10_743 ch plus the 80 ch general headroom, giving 10_823: every operation's Input, degradation notes, Output template and steps left the agent for the one reference that operation loads, so the agent now holds only the shared rules, the loading table and the routing table (target ≤ 12_000 ch). The next content addition to git.mds must fund itself with a cut elsewhere in git.mds. #712 (lean Git agent) re-derived it from a measured 10_144 ch plus the 80 ch headroom: 10_224. Lowered by #706 (lean always-loaded descriptions) to 10206.
